lesson.title: Professions and ethics
lesson.summary: In France, the titles psychologist, psychiatrist and psychotherapist and the description psychoanalyst do not imply the same training or scope of practice. This lesson explains the French framework and shows how competence, informed consent, confidentiality, rights and referral support responsible practice.
objectives: Distinguish the titles psychologist, psychiatrist and psychotherapist and the description psychoanalyst in France.
Identify the limits of a practitioner’s competence and situations that require referral.
Analyse a situation using consent, confidentiality, respect for the person and protection from abuse of power.
Distinguish legal requirements, professional rules and context-sensitive ethical decisions.
prerequisites: Define psychology as a scientific discipline.
Distinguish a field of research, a level of explanation and a setting of application.

content.text: In France, professional use of the title psychologist is protected by law and depends on specified qualifications or authorisations. A psychiatrist is a specialist physician who can make a medical diagnosis and prescribe medication. Holding the title psychologist does not in itself make someone a physician and does not authorise medication prescribing. Both professions may work in care, research, teaching or other settings depending on their training and role.

Use of the title psychotherapist is also regulated and requires registration; it is not interchangeable with psychologist or the medical specialty of psychiatry. Someone describing themselves as a psychoanalyst may also be a psychologist or psychiatrist, but this is not automatic. Each protected title, relevant qualification, registration, advertised method and actual scope of competence must therefore be checked separately.

Invented example: an occupational psychologist meets an employee who reports panic attacks and an immediate risk to her safety. The psychologist can listen, assess the situation within the limits of her role, and refer the employee to appropriate services. She must not imply that occupational training automatically covers every clinical or medical intervention. Recognising limits and arranging a referral are parts of competent practice.

Professional ethics organise responsibility towards people. The 2021 French code emphasises rights and dignity, autonomy, information, privacy, professional secrecy and confidentiality. These principles require practitioners to explain the purpose and framework of an intervention, seek free and informed consent, protect information, and limit sharing to what is justified. Applicable legal duties remain binding and must be assessed in context.

A professional title does not guarantee universal competence or the quality of a particular intervention. Before placing trust in a service, ask for the exact title, relevant training, confidentiality framework, purpose and limits, consent arrangements, and referral options. Refusing to explain the framework, guaranteeing outcomes, pressuring someone to continue, or requesting information without a clear purpose are warning signs.

concepts.description: Psychologist, psychiatrist and psychotherapist have distinct frameworks; a label alone does not establish every competence a person has.

concepts.title: Competence, limits and referral
concepts.description: Responsible practice stays within the practitioner’s training and role, explains its limits and arranges referral when needed.

concepts.title: Rights, consent and confidentiality
concepts.description: Respect for people requires information, autonomy, appropriate consent, protection of information and context-sensitive consideration of applicable duties.

tasks.title: Compare four professional descriptions
tasks.description: Create a table for psychologist, psychiatrist, psychotherapist and psychoanalyst. For each, state what the description establishes, what cannot be inferred from it, and which source you used.

tasks.title: Decide on a referral
tasks.description: Analyse three fictional situations: a learning difficulty, psychological distress that may require medical care, and a team conflict. Suggest an appropriate practitioner or service, justify the choice and identify missing information.

tasks.title: Identify ethical issues
tasks.description: In a case where an organisation requests individual questionnaire results, identify issues of purpose, information, consent, confidentiality, competence and power. Propose a safer framework in 250–350 words.

assessmentBanks.assessmentTitle: Concept check — Professional titles and roles

questions.prompt: In France, who is necessarily a physician by virtue of their title?
questions.explanation: A psychiatrist is a specialist physician. The title psychologist is not a medical title.

questions.prompt: A psychologist can prescribe medication solely by virtue of the title psychologist.
questions.explanation: A psychologist is not a physician solely by virtue of that title and cannot prescribe medication on that basis.

questions.prompt: Which titles discussed in this lesson are governed by specific French legal frameworks?
questions.explanation: Psychologist and psychotherapist are regulated by distinct texts; psychiatrist is a medical specialty.

questions.prompt: Calling oneself a psychoanalyst automatically proves that the person is also a psychologist or psychiatrist.
questions.explanation: A psychoanalyst may hold either title, but this must be checked separately.

questions.prompt: What is the most reliable response to a professional description?
questions.explanation: Check the exact title, training, relevant registration and scope of competence separately.

options.label: Check title, training, registration and competence separately
Rely only on popularity on social media

questions.prompt: A practitioner encounters a situation outside their training. What is the most responsible response?
questions.explanation: They should explain their limits and arrange an appropriate referral rather than claim universal competence.

options.label: Acknowledge the limit and suggest an appropriate referral
Avoid giving the person any explanation

questions.prompt: Holding the title psychologist means being competent in every specialty of psychology.
questions.explanation: A title does not replace the training and experience required for a particular intervention.

questions.prompt: Which information helps assess whether an intervention falls within a practitioner’s competence?
questions.explanation: Relevant training, experience, role and the nature of the need are more informative than a general label.

options.label: The nature and urgency of the need

questions.prompt: Why can referral to another professional demonstrate competence?
questions.explanation: It shows that the practitioner recognises the limits of their role and seeks an appropriate response.

options.label: It protects the person and respects professional limits
It proves the first practitioner knows nothing
It removes the need for consent

questions.prompt: What takes priority when a person faces an immediate safety risk?
questions.explanation: The urgency must be assessed and appropriate services involved under the relevant professional and legal framework.

options.label: Assess the urgency and involve appropriate services
Wait for the next appointment without acting
Publish the situation to ask for advice
Promise absolute secrecy without examining the framework

questions.prompt: What should be clarified before a psychological intervention?
questions.explanation: People need understandable information about purpose, framework, information use and relevant limits.

options.label: An obligation to accept without questions

questions.prompt: A company requests individual scores from a questionnaire presented as anonymous. What is the first problem?
questions.explanation: Individual disclosure contradicts the promise of anonymity; purpose, consent and access must be clarified.

options.label: The contradiction between promised anonymity and individual disclosure
The questionnaire must be too short
The results should be published online

questions.prompt: Consent is valid even when the person does not know the purpose or use of their data.
questions.explanation: Informed consent requires understandable information about purpose, framework and relevant consequences.
Limiting collection and access, explaining the rules and sharing only justified information reduce privacy risks.

options.label: Share the whole record by default

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the relationship between professional ethics and law?
questions.explanation: Ethical reflection guides practice, while applicable legal duties must also be identified and followed.

options.label: Professional ethics guide practice without replacing legal duties.
A professional code overrides every law.
Ethics and law are unrelated to practice.
